items.caption: This seal-script form of 下 places a short horizontal stroke below a longer one and adds a descending vertical stroke. The sources interpret the lower mark as indicating “below” and differ on when the vertical stroke became established.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 下: a long top horizontal stroke, a curved descending central stroke, and a short horizontal stroke extending right from its lower section.
items.selection_reason: The visible form gives a useful comparison with the earlier two-line indicative analysis: it retains the lower mark and adds a vertical stroke. That addition is explained as distinguishing the graph from 上 and 二, though its chronology is disputed.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw in seal-script style, not a dated artifact image. Sources disagree on whether the added vertical stroke was established in late Spring and Autumn forms or in small seal script, and no specific dated specimen is shown here.
